claims.statement: `.specify/memory/constitution.md` is the repository's single ratified source of core principles governing Frontend Apps, Backend Services, and AI Agents, and it is versioned semver-style with a change log at the top of the file recording every amendment and rationale.

The constitution currently stands at v2.7.0 (ratified 2026-03-08, last amended 2026-10-20), and the `[CURRENT]` marker at the end of the version-history block is the authoritative signal for which amendment is latest.

Constitution amendments must follow the file's Governance procedure: a proposal documenting rationale, impact and migration plan; review and formal approval; a version bump where MAJOR signals a principle change, MINOR a guidance addition and PATCH a clarification; and alignment of existing code within one release cycle.

A deviation from the constitution requires explicit human approval and a documented rationale, whereas a spec or plan may deviate from itself and simply be updated — this is the one asymmetry in the spec-driven lifecycle, so an AI assistant meeting an apparent task/constitution conflict must stop and ask rather than choose silently.

"No Vibe Coding" is a named AI Assistant Constraint requiring the assistant to always refer to the current `plan.md` and `spec.md` before writing code, with deviations requiring explicit documentation and approval — mirroring the constitution's own amendment discipline.

The Identity Provider boundary is a hard trust line: a validated, signed JWT is treated as proof the IdP already evaluated and satisfied Conditional Access and MFA, so the application must never re-implement MFA, CA checks or raw credential verification, and its authentication responsibility is limited to cryptographic token validation (signature and `iss`/`aud`/`azp`/`exp`/`nbf` claims), with authorization remaining the application's own responsibility.

The Behavior-Descriptive Identifiers principle bans requirement/specification IDs (e.g. `FR-###`, `SC-###`, `T-###`, `US#`) from code identifiers such as files, modules and exported symbols; the IDs belong in a traceability comment on the artifact, which is the one explicit exception to the prohibition on WHAT-comments.

Constitution v2.5.0 records a scoped, bounded accepted exception to the Frontend performance-budgeting rule (2-second time-to-interactive on simulated 3G) for the mcm-app web client's cold load only; it covers residual framework weight, is capped by a committed entry-chunk byte budget, and leaves the principle's JavaScript-lazy-loading clause in force.

The bounded web cold-load exception is enforced as a byte ceiling on the mcm-app web entry chunk (2,000,000 bytes against a measured 1,762,630) by `scripts/check-web-bundle-budget.mjs`, which also asserts that deferred packages are absent from the entry chunk and server-only code is absent from every client chunk.

Beyond principles, the constitution binds per-stack technology baselines and the monorepo directory structure — fixing language, framework, data-access library, container images, Nx-first task invocation, naming conventions and test placement for Backend Services, Frontend Apps and the AI Agents layer — so non-compliance is remedied by a constitution amendment or a scoped exception rather than a local convention.

The constitution's TDD mandate includes a mandatory RED-then-GREEN checkpoint format for every test task, with a Verify RED command whose expected failure output must be non-zero — a test that cannot be verified RED is not a TDD test.

Constitution v2.6.0 is a MINOR, stack-guidance-only amendment that advances the frontend baseline from Expo SDK 56 to Expo SDK 57 (React Native 0.86, React 19.2); it redefines no principle, and it was drafted in the same pull request as the dependency bump it authorises, per the rule that a version the constitution names must be amended with human approval in the change that moves it.

Only a stack element the constitution names *with a version* forces an amendment when it moves; a library named without a version does not. The frontend stack section names Tamagui and `@mcm/design-system` as the UI/styling engine but pins no version for it, so a Tamagui major is not a constitutional change, whereas the Expo SDK/native runtime, the container images and the toolchain lines are version-named and are.

Beyond principles and stack baselines the constitution carries the architecture diagrams that are the canonical picture of the runtime topology: two C4 container diagrams (multi-frontend/multi-service, and the additive AI-agents layer) and three auth-flow sequence diagrams (login, backend resource access, agent auth), the last of which specifies the RFC 8693 run-scoped subject-token exchange and downscoped backend token that keep token custody with the BFF.

Constitution v2.7.0 is a MINOR, stack-guidance-only amendment that advances the document-database baseline to `mongodb/mongodb-community-server:9.0-ubi9` (MongoDB 9.0 on Red Hat UBI 9), and it records in the changelog that the image the document had named until then, `8.2.6-ubuntu2204-slim`, was stale — `8.0.8-ubi9` is what actually ran. It redefines no principle, was operator-approved, and landed in the same pull request as the compose-file change it authorises.

A version the constitution names can itself be stale, so a version-named line is not proof of what runs: the constitution's document-database image had named a tag the stacks never ran, and the correction was recorded as part of the amendment that moved the line. A version-named line must be compared against the compose files and the lockfile before being treated as deployed truth.

Constitution compliance is operationalized per feature through a mandatory **Constitution Check** gate in every `plan.md` (the template's wording: "GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design."), which gives each principle a row with a status and how it is satisfied. Feature 081's plan is a worked example: it marks the Expo SDK line and the document-database image line as AMENDMENT REQUIRED, each naming the story that amends it, and marks the Tamagui line PASS because the constitution names that library but no version of it.

The constitution's unversioned "UI / Design System" line asserts Tamagui is "wired runtime-only by default (the Tamagui babel/metro compiler plugins are optional optimisations)", and that behavioural claim was inaccurate from feature 015 onward, which enabled `@tamagui/babel-plugin`. Feature 081 US10 restored the line's accuracy by code rather than by amendment: Tamagui 3 removed the Babel plugin, and its replacement `@tamagui/metro-plugin` 3.0.x was measured to lower some web modules to static class names without emitting their CSS while saving no bytes (entry chunk 1,881,353 B with it versus 1,881,066 B without, against the 2,000,000 B budget), so no Tamagui compiler is wired and `frontend/mcm-app/babel.config.js` runs no Tamagui plugin.

The constitution's Backend Services stack names `medi-rs` as the mandated mediator library for routing commands, queries and events from the API layer to the application-layer handler, but `backend/mc-service` ships no mediator crate: `router::build()` constructs one handler per operation over the repository traits and packs them into `AppState`, so dispatch is a direct method call on that struct. The divergence is recorded in `docs/MCM-Architecture.md` as a tracked backlog item rather than resolved by an amendment, so a constitutionally named library can be absent from the running system while the version history reads as current.

The constitution's amendment procedure is drafted through the Spec Kit constitution command (`.github/agents/speckit.constitution.agent.md`, mirrored as `.claude/skills/speckit-constitution/SKILL.md`), which loads the existing constitution, applies the MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH rule — MAJOR for a principle or governance removal or redefinition, MINOR for a new section or materially expanded guidance, PATCH for clarifications — and carries a consistency-propagation checklist that pushes the change into the dependent templates, including `.specify/templates/plan-template.md` and its spec and tasks siblings.

Feature 081 codifies the same-PR amendment rule as its governance requirement FR-015: where the governing constitution names a version the feature changes (the platform SDK and native runtime, the document-database image), the amendment MUST land in the same pull request as the change it authorises and with human approval; because the constitution names the UI styling library without a version, that story (US10) needs no amendment.
